text: Row-level security filters only ever flow in one single direction by default across any relationship — even across a relationship that's otherwise genuinely set up as fully bidirectional in your model.

One single checkbox turns that behavior on, applied individually per relationship. Reach for it specifically and deliberately when a genuine dynamic RLS scenario actually needs it — never as some kind of general-purpose fix for an unrelated filtering problem elsewhere in your model.

One real constraint genuinely worth remembering here: a table that takes part in several bidirectional relationships at once can only have this security filtering option turned on for exactly one of them, never more. And the real cost is pure performance — it can noticeably slow queries down in larger, heavily related models, so test this thoroughly before ever trusting it anywhere that actually matters.

Test as role isn't limited to checking just one single report at all — switch between reports and check every single one built on top of the same shared semantic model, not merely the very first one you happened to open.

That genuinely closes out Chapter Eleven completely, and everything this entire course teaches about securing a Power BI semantic model on purpose, rather than purely by accident of who happens to have gotten hold of a link. Chapter Twelve now puts absolutely everything you've learned together into one complete, real capstone project.
